import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 5

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/


namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture5

open SimpleGraph

variable {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nontrivial V]


open scoped Classical in
/--
WOWII [Conjecture 5](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G`, `Ls(G)` is bounded below by the maximal size
of a sphere of radius `radius(G)` around the centres of `G`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture5 (G : SimpleGraph V) (h_conn : G.Connected) :
    letI centers := { v : V | G.eccent v = G.radius }
    letI r_nat := G.radius.toNat
    letI sphere_verts (v : V) : Set V := { w | G.dist v w = r_nat }
    letI sphere_size (v : V) : ℝ := ↑(Finset.univ.filter (fun w => w ∈ sphere_verts v)).card
    letI max_sphere_size := sSup (sphere_size '' centers)
    max_sphere_size ≤ Ls G := by
  sorry

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture5

reformulations.difference: The source uses maxima of integer sphere and leaf counts. Lean casts these counts to ℝ and uses real suprema; it also converts the extended-natural graph radius to ℕ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under the hypotheses, all distances and the radius are finite, so the conversions preserve the sphere condition. The center set is nonempty and finite. Connectedness supplies a spanning tree, and there are finitely many subgraphs. Consequently both suprema are attained maxima, and casting natural cardinalities to ℝ preserves their order. In scratch Lean, the exact displayed bound was proved equivalent to the existence of a spanning tree whose number of degree-one vertices bounds every center's radius-sphere cardinality.

sources_consulted: E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjecture 5 and related remarks: https://web.archive.org/web/20260726061534id_/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html

WOWII definitions and references, particularly conjecture entry 5 and definitions 1, 9, 13, 17, 21, and 64: https://web.archive.org/web/20260723161838id_/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/wowIIdefs.js

E. DeLaVina, original November 1996 conjecture list, especially pp. 1–2, Conjecture 5 and the subsequent stronger sphere-bound remarks: https://web.archive.org/web/20230703190700id_/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII.pdf

Local definitions: FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/SpanningTree.lean; Mathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Metric.lean, Diam.lean, Subgraph.lean, Acyclic.lean, and Connectivity/Connected.lean.
review.notes: The source states exactly L_s(G) ≥ max{|S(v,rad(G))| : v is a center}, and records it as true, crediting DeLaVina and Fajtlowicz (1996); the research solved tag agrees. The explicit Nontrivial hypothesis excludes the degenerate one-vertex, radius-zero case. Checked satisfiability and the smallest admitted graph K₂: each relevant sphere has one vertex and Ls = 2. /workspace/review/final_checks.lean compiles and proves the equivalence and boundary checks without using the sorry-backed conjecture. The live cited host timed out; the source was recovered through archived copies.
